rationale: The candidate reads as a small cantilevered-and-bent object with a recognizable dominant mass, but it does not yet support the neighborhood-living contract convincingly. Across the four views, the form is only partially coherent: the top and isometric suggest one compact figure, while the front/opposite views show a pinched, over-mutated profile with collisions between the upper and lower pieces. The blue access edge is not answered by a clear public void or threshold; instead the ground condition remains mostly sealed and semantically weak. The parcel is contained, but the gesture behaves more like an abstract object than a capacity-aware mixed-use building with active edge, public court, and calm upper hierarchy. The silhouette is also too arbitrary in section, reading as repeated bends rather than a purposeful inhabited terrace or span logic. Overall, the form resembles a speculative tower-like or object mass more than a legible neighborhood ground building, so program fit fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller tower typology than the low compact neighborhood-living brief; do not copy the tower logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered upper mass can work when it sits on a clearer base and reads as one dominant object.
